bug_semantics: CWE-552 information exposure: Tainacan stores item documents under the web-accessible WordPress uploads tree at wp-content/uploads/tainacan-items/{collection_id}/{item_id}/. When an item or collection is not public, only the on-disk folder name is prefixed with the constant _x_ (TAINACAN_PRIVATE_FOLDER_PREFIX); wp_get_attachment_url / image_get_intermediate_size strip that prefix so the published URL looks like a normal uploads path. Intended access control is a post-404 PHP gate in Private_Files::template_redirect() that remaps the stripped URL onto the _x_ folder and checks Item::can_read() before readfile(). Unauthenticated attackers who request the real _x_ path (collection/item IDs are already in the public URL; the prefix is a known constant) are served the file directly by Apache/nginx because nothing at the web-server layer denied _x_ directories until 1.0.1. At 1.0.0, add_htaccess_rules() only wrote Deny from all into uploads/tainacan (logs/csv), not uploads/tainacan-items.
flaw_origin: GitHub issue #241 asked to save private attachments in a protected folder. No later commit rewrote the storage location before the 1.0.1 .htaccess.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: CVE-2025-12747 / GHSA-c6q3-c35r-7vcf is a published CWE-552, not withdrawn. Private Tainacan attachments live in wp-content/uploads/tainacan-items with an _x_ directory prefix and URL stripping; the PHP 404 handler is the only ACL, so a direct GET of the _x_ path bypasses it. That layout is first written in 8234540ec8664ce95f13d6334a51fa9a7d10da1c; the parent still used /tainacan-uploads/ outside wp-content, so the parent tree lacks the vulnerable lines (introducer_parent_absent=false after direct verification). The later class extract is a move and is not the BIC. The shipping status-based prefix in b674d860 is a refinement of the already-web-accessible _x_ scheme, not a first write. The fix that matches the advisory 1.0.0...1.0.1 boundary is 8ea7ecf14e5b31bb88a0a6a511e7ad88db84434e adding a tainacan-items .htaccess forbid rule, present in 1.0.1 and absent from 1.0.0. AI second: the BIC commit object is human (leogermani, 2019, no AI trailers), so the verdict is NOT_AI.
